Exporting to TissuePlex

Source: vignettes/articles/tissueplex-export.Rmd
tissueplex-export.Rmd

TissuePlex is an interactive viewer that draws cell-cell communication on the tissue image. NICHESv2’s part ends with one file, edges.parquet, which TissuePlex reads as an edge layer.

Write the file

export_to_TissuePlex() needs the arrow package and a spatial object. Set celltype.col to your cell type column, or NULL if you don’t have one.

library(NICHESv2)

data(NICHESv2_example)

out.file <- file.path(tempdir(), "edges.parquet")
export_to_TissuePlex(
  NICHESv2_example,
  output.path  = out.file,
  celltype.col = "celltype"
)

Every edge in $edge.list is written. Edges with signal get one row per LR pair, and edges with no signal get one placeholder row, so TissuePlex can still draw the full tissue graph.

If your coordinates aren’t in columns named x and y, set x.col and y.col.

Exporting a subset writes only the edges between kept cells.

View it in TissuePlex

Save the file as edges.parquet next to your dataset, then follow the TissuePlex documentation from there:

  • User manual: installation and loading your data.
  • Worked examples: full walkthroughs.

TissuePlex needs your platform’s own output files as well, such as the tissue image. These come from your data, not from NICHESv2.
